title: Give each job a read-only evidence snapshot and athena status --snapshot
summary: At dispatch, Athena writes a read-only snapshot outside the working copy holding records/ and main's first-parent log (hash, commit time, subject, trailers). The producer and verifier briefs name its path, and `athena status` gains an option to read records and history from it. The audience is producers and verifiers who currently cannot check real-records criteria.

defaults_applied.how: New tests for dispatch snapshot, status parity, and briefs; fmt, clippy and test pass.
Criteria run dispatch and status and check the snapshot's contents and output, not that files exist.
Outcome is that a job can check real-records criteria from the snapshot.
Read-only is enforced by file permissions and tested.
Criterion forbids secrets or personal data in the snapshot code and tests.
One focused change across the listed files.
Tests exercise the dispatch path and the status option.
Briefs and CHANGELOG written for an outside reader.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: I only grepped crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs (dispatch at ~line 684), crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs (producer_brief ~415, verifier_brief ~983) and crates/athena-cli/src/main.rs (Command::Status ~314, handler ~1211); the producer must read them and status.rs fully. The snapshot is written during dispatch before the producer starts, then the brief inputs carry its path. Status loads records and history from the main checkout today and must load them from the snapshot dir when the option is given. The snapshot holds a copy of records/ in the same layout plus a history file; it is plain files, not a record kind under crates/athena-data, so no new AnyRecord variant or check_record_file entry is expected. If the producer adds one, it must be covered by the round-trip test. Throughput is measured directly by comparing the rendered throughput section from both sources on the same records.

Prior jobs: 20261029-233021-e5sg (rejected) and 20261029-210827-18fc (landed) are the motivating evidence only. This job does not redo the landing-stage fix or the build-measurement work; their landed or rejected files are neither kept nor changed here. The e5sg landing-matching findings and the 18fc sccache-isolation finding are left to their own follow-ups, since this job only supplies the evidence they needed.

The snapshot lives under the job's directory in Athena's state area (outside the working copy), is created at dispatch, and is made read-only by file permissions (dirs 0555, files 0444). The working copy still has no records/.
The option name is `--snapshot <path>` on `athena status`, and it takes the snapshot root. History is stored as a text or JSON file in a documented format that status parses.
Governance files: athena.toml, defaults.toml and workflow files do not need to change. Briefs are composed in code, so prompt-token budgets are not touched.
The history log is first-parent on main at dispatch, capped to a reasonable number of commits. Records are copied as of dispatch.

acceptance_criteria.text: A test through the real dispatch path (run `cargo test -p athena-core`) shows the snapshot directory exists at the path the briefs name, is read-only (write attempts fail or permissions are non-writable), contains the records copied at dispatch, and contains main's first-parent history (hash, commit time, subject, trailers) at dispatch.
A test (run `cargo test -p athena-core status`) shows `athena status` run against the snapshot gives a throughput section identical to the one from the main checkout for the same records and history.
A CLI test (run `cargo test -p athena-cli`) shows `athena status --snapshot <dir>` reads records and history from the snapshot and does not need a records/ directory in the current working directory.

Tests in crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs (run `cargo test -p athena-context`) show that both the producer and verifier briefs state the snapshot path and say that real-records checks use it. The working copy remains without records/.

The change is limited to crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs, crates/athena-core/src/status.rs, crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs, crates/athena-cli/src/main.rs and CHANGELOG.md, plus any test files or helper modules they require (checked with git diff --stat).
`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test` all pass.
CHANGELOG.md has a new entry describing the evidence snapshot and the `athena status` snapshot option.
No secrets or personal data are written into the snapshot code, tests or docs, and the snapshot is not added to git history.

out_of_scope: Redoing the landing-stage matching fix from job 20261029-233021-e5sg (its store.rs and athena-git changes are dropped here)
Isolating sccache statistics per measurement (finding from job 20261029-210827-18fc); its landed files are kept as landed
Putting records/ into the producer's working copy
Changing athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflow files or records/
Changing how the throughput section is computed
departures: Higher cost and time than reference because the change spans dispatch, briefs, status and CLI with a filesystem-permission test.
urgent_reason: Cuts failed and rejected attempts: jobs 20261029-233021-e5sg and 20261029-210827-18fc failed or stalled because records could not be checked from a job's working copy.
hard_reason: Changes the run pipeline (dispatch and the briefs given to producer and verifier) and how verification evidence is supplied, so a mistake is costly and hard to see.
